Goose Goose Duck

Every goose
has a story.

A group of friends plays Goose Goose Duck every Saturday and streams it to YouTube. Every game below was read back from the end-of-game screen in those recordings: no game files, memory or network traffic involved.

How the group played

Who took the wins, and which roles won most often.

Honour board

What about me?

Compare with other players

Pick a dot and the card above switches to that player.

?

Further right means more games played; higher means a higher win rate. The percentage scale zooms in on the range where most games fall. Dots outside it sit on the top or bottom edge with an arrow; the exact result shows on hover and once the dot is selected. The main part of the table lists players with 50+ games all-time. The side filter changes the numbers but not this threshold. Smaller samples are moved to the bottom. The dashed line is the median of personal win rates among players with 50+ games all-time and at least one game in the selected slice. Every player counts equally. The light band around the median is where the win rate of a player who plays exactly at the median would land with that many games (95%).

All players — table
As a goose and as a duck

Each player's win rate as a goose and as a duck. The dashed lines are each side's level across the group; the whiskers show where a rate could land with this many games. Players with 60+ games as a goose and 20+ as a duck; tap a name to open their card.

Rankings and roles

Roles and wins

?

Win rate among the times the role was dealt, for the selected side. Roles dealt 20+ times are shown. This is how players with the role did, not proof the ability is useful: team, map and lobby settings all play a part.

Which neutrals won most

?

Win rate among all the times the role was dealt. A role could appear more than once in a game. Roles dealt at least 5 times are compared.

Every neutral gets a stage

?

Sorted by win rate among players with at least 5 games as the selected role. Ties break on number of games, then name. Smaller samples are shown separately.
